tools.name: document-write
tools.title: Create, edit, delete, restore, move, or share a Cedar doc
tools.description: Cedar Docs: persistent agent-curated documents. ACTIONS: (1) write: upsert (replace), append, or patch. Types: document, workflow, html, agenda, conversation_agenda, attachment. If load-skill lists "documents", load it FIRST for the correct AOP template; otherwise write plain markdown. (2) delete: hide by documentId from document-read output. Interactive chat proposes this and waits for approval: explain the removal, never claim completion early. Autonomous surfaces (cron, external MCP, bots) apply immediately. (3) restore: undo deletion by documentId within 30 days. Org KB docs may be deleted by any org member; other unowned docs, PLAYBOOK.md, playbook resources and subagents are protected. (4) move: relocate between virtual paths, e.g. promote a thread artifact to persistent scope. (5) share: generate/revoke a public token-gated link. Requires a live user; publishing is a person's decision. (6) request-file: show a picker for a needed Google Drive file; relay the result rather than saying no picker is available. Chat writes attach/open automatically; never tell the UI to show one. Put params only in the object named for the action, e.g. action:"write", write:{...}. Read and update personal chat instructions at #chat-agent (user/playbooks/CHAT_AGENT.md); patch existing rules, or upsert if missing when saving a standing instruction. Read back to verify. Load documents skill before non-trivial paths or shortcuts (#kb, #wiki, #playbook, #here, #sections, #outline, #section/Name, #lines/a-b). Workflow: inert JSON fences with clickable buttons. Load documents skill for authoring; discover eligible mutation inputs with workflow.list_operations. Saving never executes buttons.

action.description: Which write to perform — pass its matching params object below (e.g. action: "write" pairs with write: {...}).

path.description: Virtual path for the document. Path encodes scope and name; see Cedar Docs guidance for path conventions and supported shortcuts.

type.description: Behavioural type for the document. "document" = Y.js markdown (default for all text). "workflow" = markdown with actionable workflow JSON fences; saving never executes buttons. "html" = self-contained HTML blob rendered as iframe (use for presentations, reports). "agenda" = Y.js + task sync for the user daily agenda. "conversation_agenda" = Y.js + task sync for a per-conversation agenda. "attachment" = file reference (no content; details in metadata). "table" = spreadsheet, rendered as a data grid; only for CREATING one or rewriting it whole (frontmatter schema + one pipe table with a leading _id column) — use the `table` tool for every partial read/write, because a partial write routed through here rewrites every row and destroys row identity.

tools.name: table
tools.title: Manage Cedar tables
tools.description:
Read/edit row-addressed Cedar tables. Load the tables skill first. Read before writing; never recreate a table to edit it.

ACTIONS (pass the matching params object):
read: pipe rows, revision and full schema; project columns/rowIds/where/limit; orderBy sorts by column type.
create: declare labeled columns; from materializes rows from a real query.
add_columns: add labeled columns, optionally after a key.
update_columns: [{key,patch}] in columns; stable keys, omitted settings preserved, null clears optional settings.
remove_columns: keys to remove, including cells.
reorder_columns: every key exactly once.
update_view: patch viewFilter, sort, subrowColumns, titleColumn or purpose; null clears optional settings.
add_rows: one pipe row per line.
set: one rowId.columnKey = value per line; unknown rowId creates a row only with titleColumn assigned.
clear: same addresses, no values; keeps rows.
delete_rows: by rowId.
move_row: rowId, beforeRowId (null appends), required ifRevision; no active sort/subrows.
insert_section: heading above/below anchorRowId.
export: csv/xlsx file bytes as base64, using the UI export pipeline.
import: uploaded xlsx/csv; updateInPlace merges by _id.
fill: one agent per row; >25 needs user confirmation. mode=delegate means YOU run briefs in parallel; spawned means Cedar runs them.
bindings: built-in and account field paths.

Bound columns are read-only: never set/fill one. Address rows by rowId; ordinals/A1 need ifRevision. Subrows: childId._parent = parentId. Section rows (_section) hold headings only; never fill them. Bulk strings use one record per line, not JSON arrays.

action.description: Which verb to run — pass its matching params object below (e.g. action: "set" pairs with set: {assignments}).

path.description: Virtual path of the table document, e.g. "conversation/{id}/pipeline-review" or "#kb/q3-accounts". Supports the same path shortcuts as the document tool.

columns.description: Column keys to project. Omit for all columns.

rowIds.description: Specific rows, returned in the order asked. Omit for all rows; mutually exclusive with `where`.

where.description: One `columnKey op value` per line, ANDed. Ops: =, !=, contains, empty, notempty.

offset.description: 0-based row offset for the next page.

orderBy.description: Order the page by one column, the way its TYPE orders — currency numerically, a date by the instant, a select by its declared option order, `_status` by the fan-out lifecycle. Empty cells are always last. Applied after `where` and before paging, so `orderBy` + `limit` is a real top-N. Ordinal and A1 addressing still resolve against DOCUMENT order, so write back by _id.

viewFilter.description: Persistent view filter; descendants inherit visibility unless matchDescendants is true. Does not delete records.

subrowColumns.description: Independent child-row layout. Declare these keys in columns, optionally hidden there; labels and widths can differ from parent rows.

hidden.description: Hide from parent rows; still available in subrowColumns.

label.description: Required, non-empty, unique. The rendered header, e.g. "Next step date".

key.description: Stable lower-snake handle used in every `set` line (`r_07.next_step`). Minted from the label when omitted, and IMMUTABLE afterwards — renaming a column changes only its label.

type.description: Cell type; defaults to text. conversation/task/draft/doc/person/company hold a `[[type: id]]` reference token and render as a live chip.

description.description: One-line human description, shown on header hover.

fillInstruction.description: How to derive this cell. This is the column's real payload for a fan-out — each row-scoped subagent is handed the fillInstruction of every column it owns.

required.description: Cells must be non-empty before a row counts as done.

binding.description: Derive this cell instead of writing it. `<refColumnKey>.<field>` reads through THAT column's reference cell (`deal.stage`, `their_company.domain`, `deal.fields.<fieldKey>`) and errors per row if the cell holds another kind of reference; `<entity>.<field>` is shorthand for the row's first ref of that entity, which is only unambiguous while there is one. Recomputed rather than edited, and READ-ONLY — never `set` a bound column or hand one to `fill`. Call `bindings` for every path this table can use.

options.description: select / multi_select only. ORDER MATTERS: the declared order is the order the picker lists them in AND the order the column sorts by, so declare them along whatever progression the column measures (earliest → latest, worst → best, coldest → warmest), not in the order they occurred to you.

outputKind.description: output only. Which artifact this column produces — a column that declares none cannot be filled.

format.description: date only. date-fns format; defaults to yyyy-MM-dd.

columns.description: Ordered column list. At least one.

titleColumn.description: Column key that labels a row. Defaults to the first column. `set` refuses to create a row unless this column is assigned in the same call.

purpose.description: Why the table exists. Shown as a subtitle and fed to filling agents.

schema.description: The table schema. Columns are always declared and always headed — there are no anonymous columns.

rows.description: Optional initial rows, one pipe row per line — same grammar as add_rows.

source.description: Where rows come from. `conversations` and `tasks` are supported.

filter.description: Same filter surface as find-crm-conversations — not a second query language.

intoColumn.description: Column that receives the [[<source>: id]] ref. Defaults to the first reference column.

from.description: Materialize rows from a real query instead of transcribing them. USE THIS whenever the row set comes from Cedar data — "every deal closing this quarter", "all my customers".

description.description: Short summary shown in document listings.

after.description: Insert after this column key. Omit to append.

label.description: Required, non-empty, unique. The rendered header, e.g. "Next step date".

ifRevision.description: Revision from read; rejects concurrent schema edits.

rows.description:
One GFM pipe row per line. Leading cell is the rowId; `-` mints one. Cell count after the id must equal the column count exactly — write an empty cell as `| |`.
  - | Globex | [[conversation: 44a1…]] | |
  r_07 | Initech | | [[draft: r-99]] |

assignments.description:
One `<rowRef>.<columnKey> = <value>` per line:
  r_07.outreach = [[draft: r-3821]]   ← stable rowId, always safe
  acme.company  = Acme Corp           ← unknown rowId → the row is created
  4.outreach    = Sent                ← 1-based data-row ordinal, needs ifRevision
  D4            = Sent                ← A1-style, needs ifRevision
Values are cell markdown; `\|` is a literal pipe and a trailing `\` continues onto the next line.

ifRevision.description: The `revision` a previous `read` returned. REQUIRED when any line addresses a row by ordinal or A1; the whole call is rejected if the document has moved since. Never needed for rowId-addressed lines.

targets.description: One cell address per line, same addressing as `set`, with no value: `r_07.outreach`. Empties the cell; the row stays.

updateInPlace.description: Merge into the table already at `path` instead of creating one: rows are matched by their `_id`, so a Cedar export the user edited in Excel updates the rows it changed and leaves every other row untouched. Requires a table to already exist there.

tools.name: config-read
tools.title: Read Cedar configuration
tools.description: For "why didn't X happen"/system-behavior questions, load-skill('cedar-configuration') first — these actions read raw config, they don't explain behavior. ACTIONS: (1) read-playbook — mode="list"/"load_full"/"load_sections" of an AOP's PLAYBOOK.md, by aopId or aopName. load_full/load_sections also return the org playbook as `orgPlaybook` (a user-level-only read can miss real trigger/subagent wiring). mode: "list" also gives the caller's own AOPs (name/id/hasPlaybook/isNoOp). (2) read-settings — CRM/Slack connections (incl. connectionId, needed by apply-change) + user settings. (3) list-fields — every field's definition, mapping, and options (custom + built-in). MUST load-skill('cedar-configuration', 'fields-and-values') first — it has the full rules this omits. (4) list-org-members — the caller's own org directory (id/name/email), optionally filtered by `search`; use it for a teammate's userId instead of querying the user table. (5) find-bot-slack-channels — every Slack channel Cedar's bot can actually post to, optionally filtered by `nameFilter`. Use before authoring any new Slack delivery target, never a runtime lookup left in prose. Admin/owner sees every channel the bot is in; a regular member sees only ones they're also in. Not a personal notification destination (that's `notify`'s list-slack-channels) — answers "can Cedar deliver here", not "where does this rep want their own alerts". Each action takes its params in a same-named object (e.g. action: "read-playbook" pairs with a readPlaybook: {...} object) — omit every params object except the one matching your chosen action.

mode.description: "list" — discover the user's AOPs (name/id/hasPlaybook/isNoOp/selectionProcedure/customAssignmentInstruction/orgAssignmentInstruction/effectiveAssignmentInstruction), optionally filtered by aopName. "load_full" — read the full PLAYBOOK.md for one AOP, plus its org-level playbook (`orgPlaybook`) if one exists, plus an `editMap`: every referenced subagent/resource and each inline PLAYBOOK.md surface, tagged with `source` (user|org) + `writeTarget`. To edit playbook behavior, write to a target's `writeTarget` — do NOT choose user-vs-org scope by hand. "load_sections" — read only the named sections of one AOP's playbook (and the same sections of its org-level playbook if one exists), plus the same `editMap` (requires `sections`).

aopId.description: Explicit AOP ID to target for load_full/load_sections. Omit to use the conversation currently in context, or resolve by aopName instead.

aopName.description: AOP name to target instead of aopId (e.g. "Deals"). For mode="list", filters the returned list (case-insensitive; no match returns an empty list, not an error). For load_full/load_sections, resolves to an aopId via list-aops (case-insensitive exact match, then substring) — if nothing matches, the call fails explicitly rather than silently falling back to the conversation in context.

sections.description: Required for mode="load_sections". Section header names (without the "## " prefix) to extract, e.g. ["Stages", "Objection Handling"]. Each is matched independently and the results are concatenated.

targetUserId.description: Org owner/admin only: read another org member's playbook (theirs, not yours) — pass their userId. When set, mode="list" returns THAT member's AOPs (use it to find their aopId), and load_full/load_sections read their playbook. Pass an explicit aopId/aopName alongside it; the conversation-in-context fallback is yours, not theirs. Omit to read your own. Rejected for non-admins or a target outside your org.
Org owner/admin only: target a same-org member. Omit for self; non-admins and cross-org targets are rejected.

userId.description: DEPRECATED alias for targetUserId. Same authorization gate; prefer targetUserId.

sections.description: Which sections to load. "data_services" returns provider defaults, policy origins, versions, watcher defaults and credential availability (never secrets). "connections" returns the connectionId required by apply-change's CRM/Slack change types — call this before apply-change whenever you need one and don't already have it. "user_settings" includes agentExecutionEnabled/pushDraftsToExternalClient for visibility, but neither is settable from any tool: they are not fields on any apply-change change type, and agentExecutionEnabled is additionally writable only by Cedar staff. Report them; never try to change them. "inboxes" returns custom inbox tabs, layout, and shared inboxSortingInstructions (read before changing sorting preferences or managing inbox tabs). "task_groups" returns the task lanes (get group ids before a manage_task_group update/delete/reorder). "credentials" returns the stored credential entries this user can reach (own + org): name, scope, instructions and which FIELD NAMES are stored. Never values.

aopId.description: A user AOP id. Always returns both this AOP's own fields and its linked org AOP's fields, if any.

targetUserId.description: Org owner/admin only: target a same-org member user AOP (scope=user). Omit for self; non-admins and cross-org targets are rejected.

targetUserIds.description: View MANY reps at once instead of just yourself — orthogonal to `targetUserId` above (that names ONE teammate to act as; this names a SET to view). Omit for your own fields only (unchanged default). An explicit array of userIds, or the literal "org" for every rep on this SAME AOP type — every user AOP linked to the same org AOP as `aopId`, not everyone in the organization. Naming anyone other than yourself requires org-admin authorization (aop_field:org) and is refused otherwise.

rollup.description: true summarizes across every targeted rep — uniform/diverging/missing per field key, vs. the org default — instead of returning each rep's raw field list. Defaults to false when exactly one rep is targeted (returns the same flat field list as omitting `targetUserIds` entirely), true when more than one is. Pass explicitly to override either default.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring match on a member's name OR email. Omit to list everyone.

nameFilter.description: Case-insensitive substring match on the channel name. Omit to list everything.

user_request_summary.description: One sentence, in your own words: what the user actually asked you to do in this turn. Used only for Cedar's observability — it does not change what this tool does.

is_new_request.description: true on the FIRST Cedar tool call of a NEW user request; false when this call continues the same request you are already working on. Groups related calls into one activity thread.

renameTrackingId.description: Internal rename-tracking identifier — NOT a query key. Use the field's `fieldKey` (one level up on this list-fields entry) for run-sql's `field_id` or a `wm_<fieldKey>` filter (e.g. "close_date"); this is an opaque, unrelated string (e.g. "cf_field_a1b2c3d4-..."), not a derivable variant of `fieldKey`. A couple of internal code paths (delete-field, remove-field-option) currently key lookups off this identifier instead of `fieldKey` — that is a known bug, not a second valid way to reference the field.

researchPrompt.description: For the built-in people field: who Multi-thread should research and which sources to use; never outreach.

ownerAgentId.description: Owning subagent's agent_id. Set = only that agent writes it.

tools.title: Update Cedar configuration
tools.description: For "why didn't X happen"/system-behavior questions, load-skill('cedar-configuration') first — these actions write/mutate raw config, they don't explain behavior. ACTIONS: (1) reassign-aop — re-evaluate/reassign a conversation's AOP. (2) create-field — add a custom field. tools.description:
Execute a read-only SQL SELECT query against the Cedar CRM database.

The primary path for analytical questions about the pipeline — any aggregation, filter or join,
e.g. "which objection themes separate won from lost deals?".

**Call first**: `load-skill("run-sql")` — REQUIRED before any query (column meanings, join
shapes, rejected query shapes + rewrites — not repeated here). Also `taxonomy-fields` for what
happened INSIDE calls/emails (objections, discovery, pain, MEDDPICC) — org fields no CRM column
holds.

**Rules**:
- SELECT only (`WITH ... SELECT` CTEs are fine); anything else is rejected.
- Only these tables, incl. subqueries/CTEs: agent_executions, agent_operating_procedures, calendar_events, crm_call_events, crm_companies_global, crm_company_relationships, crm_conversation_companies, crm_conversation_contacts, crm_conversation_field_values, crm_conversation_updates, crm_conversation_users, crm_conversations, crm_custom_events, crm_email_events, crm_events, crm_meeting_events, crm_note_events, crm_people_global, crm_slack_messages, documents, user, user_tasks. Enforced
  by parsing, not documentation.
- Every table with an org column needs a real `WHERE`/`JOIN...ON` predicate scoping it to
  your organization (e.g. `crm_conversations.organization_id = '<your org id>'`), AND'd in —
  a UUID elsewhere in the text doesn't count. Don't know your org ID? Run any query first: the
  rejection names your real one for the next call (never an argument; SQL text is the one place
  it appears).
- Tables with no org column must join one that has it, via a real foreign key.
- Capped at 500 rows/30s. Aggregate in SQL; for verbatim moments, take ids to `conversation-read`.

tools.name: conversation-read
tools.title: Read CRM conversations
tools.description: CRM conversation read/query over Cedar's OWN records (NOT the connected external CRM — that's action 4; ask if unclear). ACTIONS: (1) get — fetch a conversation by ID (brief timeline default; write_to_file for full content; expandEventId to inline one event); email entries include observed open/click tracking summaries when available. (2) find — locate Cedar conversations via `filters` (field/operator/value, ANDed): standard columns, computed booleans, or custom fields as "wm_<fieldKey>"; add extraFields for more columns. Call load-skill("conversation") for the full field reference. (3) search-semantic — vector/FTS search over conversation content (Turbopuffer); best for finding WHICH events matter. For ONE named call/email, do not answer from hits (a top-k slice, not the full transcript) — resolve its eventId here or via get's timeline, then re-read it whole via (1) get with expandEventId. (4) search-external-crm-deals — search the connected EXTERNAL CRM for a deal by keyword (get providerId from config read-settings first). DEAL-INTELLIGENCE (over extracted sub-event taxonomy atoms): (5) timeline — one time-ordered stream across events + both taxonomy planes for 1+ deals, filtered by fieldIds/kinds/stages/reps/scores/payload/time. (6) field-evolution — one field's series over time, grouped by deal. (7) value-as-of — a versioned field's value+scores at a stage/date/event. (8) describe-field — a field's plane/scores/vocab/payload keys (learn before filtering). (9) raw-content — resolve a deal's RAW verbatim events to a doc-sink buffer (stage-marked); read via read-document (#lines/#words) + search-documents (regex). (10) search — semantic search over the atoms (same cube); hits point back. Large results → the doc sink. Pass each action's params in a same-named object; omit the others.

Personal reminders never schedule automatic agent execution. complete: mark done. delete: dismiss/delete; draft deletion needs authorization. updateDueDate: edit date. start: prepare caller-owned work in the current Cedar chat; follow seedPrompt. Does not execute or send. Recommendations stay recommended; no accept action. Never impersonate teammates. applyApproval: apply an exact saved CRM approval on user request; await CRM confirmation, no agent fallback. Apply all: list scope="#crm-approvals", apply sequentially, report failures. list: own active tasks by conversation or scope="#today"/"#overdue"; groups/outputKinds filters, includeRecommended=true for proposals. create: requires a real deal for automatic drafting via agentExecutionEnabled. dueDate="NOW" allowed for non-agent tasks without a future blocker. update: edit/reschedule/toggle execution/mark done; cleanupDraft=true removes stale draft on completion. cancel: obsolete tasks by IDs/age/conversation. Current-run tasks protected from update/cancel. assignmentOptions: owners, authority, assignmentVersion, draft-reset needs, pendingTransfer. reassign: get options; needs owner/deal-owner/admin authority. Reuse draft-deletion approval and UUID idempotencyKey; recover pendingTransfer. Finishing is pending. Completion attempts assignee Slack DM with task link unless self-assigned/disabled. Never call notify-user (targets actor). Confirm transfer only; say Slack delivery is unconfirmed unless verified.

description.description: The task, in TWO parts separated by an em dash: a short bolded-in-the-UI headline, then the detail. `<headline> — <detail>`. Plain text only — no markdown, no asterisks, no bullets, no line breaks; the UI paints the two halves itself and shows the raw characters if you add any. The headline is 3-8 words and names the commitment ("Send Simon the pricing recap"); the detail is ONE sentence saying why it is owed or what it needs, in the second person ("you told him you would send it before the 4:30, and the deck is still unattached"). Never name the deal in either half — the UI renders the deal as a badge next to the headline, so writing it makes the row say it twice. Examples: "Amie is waiting on eDocs naming — she answered your question about starting with two doc-heavy carriers; the reply is yours", "Book the Bukaty pricing call — Natalie confirmed Friday 2:00 but you still owe the policy counts for both offices". Omit the dash and the detail only when the headline is the whole truth ("Renew the SOC2 questionnaire").

notes.description: Additional context for agent/human execution. E.g., "Mention Q4 timeline discussion from last meeting". Only execution related instructions should be here, dont include reasons for scheduling/etc.

taskChannel.description: How this task will be carried out: email, slack, linkedin or whatsapp. Only set it when the channel is genuinely part of the commitment — "reply to this thread" is an email by definition. For open-ended work like "follow up with Sarah", LEAVE IT UNSET: you do not know today whether that follow-up should be an email or a Slack message, and by the time it comes due a channel may exist that does not exist now. An unset channel is decided at execution, with better information; a guessed one is recorded as fact and biases whoever picks the task up.

tools.name: mail
tools.title: Read email
tools.description: Mail operations. ACTIONS: (1) fetch-attachments — download and read email attachment content by Gmail message ID. Pass messageId (from "Message ID:" on the email) and optionally attachmentId to fetch one file. (2) list-sent — fetch emails the Cedar agent drafted that were actually sent, to compare drafted vs. sent bodies. Use maxSimilarity < 0.7 to find emails the user rewrote significantly. Each result's messageId can be passed straight into fetch-attachments to pull its attachments (null for older rows). (3) find — query sent/received emails by STRUCTURED criteria: direction (inbound/outbound), has attachments, sender, subject/snippet substring, date range. Use this instead of semantic search when you need emails matching specific metadata — e.g. "sent emails with attachments", "emails from X last week". Returns messageId values you can pass straight into fetch-attachments. (4) search-live — search the user's LIVE Gmail mailbox by full Gmail query syntax (search.messages-style, e.g. "from:jane@acme.com newer_than:30d has:attachment"); returns thread ids + subject/from/snippet. Use this (not find/search-semantic) for mail that may never have synced, or when you need the freshest state. (5) read-thread — read a full email thread LIVE from the mailbox by threadId (from search-live), including per-message observed open/click counts, timestamps, tracking-enabled flags and full event history with observed IP addresses when available. NOTE: for semantic (meaning-based) search over ALREADY-SYNCED mail, use conversation.search-semantic with filters.eventType: "email"; search-live is a raw live-mailbox query instead. Each action takes its params in a same-named object (e.g. action: "fetch-attachments" pairs with a fetchAttachments: {messageId} object) — omit every params object except the one matching your chosen action.

tools.name: meetings
tools.title: Read & sync meetings
tools.description: Meeting operations. ACTIONS: (1) find — locate meetings Cedar has already synced, by title, attendee (email / domain / name), organizer, date range, or a pasted meeting/recording LINK. Works identically for every provider because it reads Cedar's store, not the provider's API — none of which support title search. Use this FIRST whenever the user references a call ("the pricing discussion", "the call with Jane last week") or pastes a Fathom/Circleback link. (2) sync — pull a meeting that never reached Cedar from the connected recorder (Fathom, Circleback, Granola, Gong, …) and attach it to a deal. Providers only accept a days-back window, so narrow with titleContains / participant / url; 0 or 2+ matches syncs nothing and returns candidates to disambiguate with the user. (3) capabilities — what this user's recorder can actually do and how to search it well. Call before an expensive or possibly-impossible hunt (searching what was SAID, a wide date range, or after sync came back empty); not needed for ordinary lookups, since find and sync take the same parameters and return the same answers whichever recorder is connected. Each action takes its params in a same-named object — omit every params object except the one matching your chosen action.

tools.name: calendar
tools.title: View & modify calendar events
tools.description: Work with the user's Google Calendar. ACTIONS: (1) list-events — fetch events in a time range, enriched with linked CRM conversation info. (2) get-availability — check busy periods across the user's calendars before proposing meeting times. (3) modify-event — CREATE, UPDATE, or DELETE a calendar event (pick via the operation param: "create" needs summary/startDateTime/endDateTime/attendees; "update" needs eventId + the fields to change; "delete" needs eventId). Pass `recurrence` (RFC 5545 RRULE strings) to send a repeating invite. Before rescheduling or editing an existing event, check `canModifyForEveryone` from list-events — when it is false the user does NOT own the event and cannot move it for the other guests; modify-event will refuse the change, and you must offer to ask the organizer or propose times instead. In the in-app chat, modify-event streams a proposal card for the user to approve. On every other surface (external MCP, bots, automations) it applies the change immediately (creating/updating/deleting the real event and notifying attendees) — the calling client is the approval layer. Each action takes its params in a same-named object (e.g. action: "modify-event" pairs with a modifyEvent: {...} object) — omit every params object except the one matching your chosen action.

action.description: Which operation to perform — pass its matching params object below (e.g. action: "modify-event" pairs with modifyEvent: {...}).

timeMin.description: Start of time range in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2026-03-01T00:00:00-07:00). Required — the beginning of the period to fetch events for. If no clear input is provided, use the FIRST DAY of the current year.

timeMax.description: End of time range in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2026-03-01T23:59:59-07:00). Required — the end of the period to fetch events for. If no clear input is provided, use the LAST DAY of the current year.

calendarId.description: Calendar ID to fetch events from. Defaults to 'primary'. Only pass a different value if the user explicitly asks about a specific calendar.

q.description: Free text search query. Filters events by matching against title, description, location, and attendee names/emails.

startDateTime.description: Start of time range to check availability in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-03-15T00:00:00-07:00). Should be the beginning of the day or time range you want to check.

endDateTime.description: End of time range to check availability in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-03-15T23:59:59-07:00). Should be the end of the day or time range you want to check.

calendarIds.description: Optional array of calendar IDs to check. If not provided, uses the user's selected calendars from their calendar settings, or falls back to 'primary' calendar.

operation.description: Which calendar mutation to perform. "create" needs summary/startDateTime/endDateTime/attendees. "update" needs eventId plus any fields you want to change. "delete" needs only eventId.

eventId.description: The Google Calendar event ID to update or delete. Required for operation=update/delete.

summary.description: Meeting title. Required for create. For update, provide only to change it. Use format "CompanyName <> CompanyName" if companies are clear, or "FirstName <> FirstName" if not.

description.description: Meeting description. For create, defaults to empty. If there is an agreed next topic, provide 2-3 bullet points.

startDateTime.description: Start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-03-15T10:00:00-07:00). Required for create. MUST be in the future.

endDateTime.description: End time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2024-03-15T11:00:00-07:00). Required for create. MUST be after startDateTime.

attendees.description: Meeting attendees. Required for create. CRITICAL: ONLY include attendees whose ACTUAL email addresses you extracted from the conversation (headers, signatures, previous messages). ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: making up emails or using placeholder domains (@example.com, @domain.com). Better to have fewer real attendees than fake ones.

location.description: Meeting location. For create, defaults to "Online" for virtual meetings.

wantsMeetLink.description: Whether to create a video conference link. For create, defaults to true when omitted, so leave it out. Pass false ONLY if the user explicitly asked for no video link or said the meeting is in person with no call. If they asked for a link, keep it even when the meeting is at an office. Never pass false on your own judgement.

conferenceType.description: Which conference `wantsMeetLink` creates: `hangoutsMeet` (Google Meet, the default) or `zoom`, which Cedar mints on the user's own Zoom account and attaches to the event. Only set `zoom` when the user asked for Zoom by name; a user who has not connected Zoom gets an event with no video link rather than a failure.

recurrence.description: RFC 5545 recurrence rules to make this a repeating event, e.g. ["RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO;COUNT=10"]. Omit for a one-time event. Common patterns: daily "RRULE:FREQ=DAILY", weekly "RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR", biweekly "RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2", monthly "RRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY". Add ";COUNT=n" to stop after n occurrences, or ";UNTIL=YYYYMMDD" to stop on a date — do not set both. tools.name: board
tools.title: Manage Cedar boards
tools.description:
A kanban whose CARDS are documents — a path, a share link, a `[[doc: id]]` address. The board is a FILE and knows nothing about what it is for. A card is a title, a description and a flat bag of `fields`; the board's `fields[]` declares which keys exist and their types.

COLUMNS ARE A VIEW, never a card property. `view.groupByField` names the field whose VALUES are the columns: point it at `status` and columns are statuses, at `owner` and the SAME cards regroup — no card changed. `move` writes that field. Empty draws under `__ungrouped__` unless the field sets a `default`.

ACTIONS
 list_boards · read · get_schema · list_templates — what exists · a board + cards · its schema · starting schemas.
 create_board — from a list_templates id, or empty (a placeholder axis your `fields` replace).
 set_schema — THE HEADLINE VERB: fields, view, `triggers`, anything under `meta`. MERGES; replace:true wipes. add_fields/set_view/set_board_meta edit narrowly.
 list_triggers — what fires this board and what it fires on a move. Authored via set_schema `triggers`.
 add_card · set · move · comment · archive — file · edit (fields MERGE) · column/order · append · delete.
 cards — search every board (omit `board`) or one: by column, field value, substring.

SET GLYPHS WHEN YOU CREATE THE BOARD. A select field may carry `optionIcons`, one per value, e.g. {backlog:"circle-dashed",done:"circle-check"}. Names: circle-dashed circle circle-dot circle-check circle-x circle-slash inbox play pause eye clock flag alert. Unknown names draw nothing.

THE SCHEMA IS YOURS AND OPEN. Invent fields, a view, triggers, a `meta` block — unknown keys survive verbatim, an unknown `type` (e.g. "sentiment") is kept and drawn as text. Refused only: a reserved key of the wrong SHAPE, or >64KB.

ADOPTION: a card naming an undeclared field ADDS it — check `adopted`.

board.description: Board name, path, or id. Required for every verb except list_boards, set, move, comment.

card.description: Card path or id. Required for set, move, comment.

default.description: Value a card gets for this field when `add_card` omits the key — e.g. "backlog" on `status`, so a card filed with no status IS a Backlog card on disk rather than landing ungrouped. Most useful on the field `view.groupByField` points at.

metrics.description: Median seconds between consecutive direction-changing events (their reply latency).
Median seconds between consecutive outbound emails (follow-up cadence).
Median seconds from a meeting to the next email (post-meeting recap latency).
Share of deals (with an outbound email) that drew an inbound reply.
Number of events matching the filter (activity volume).
Funnel — count of DISTINCT deals that reached each stage (a deal reached stage X if any of its events is stamped stage_at_time=X). Groups by stage; ignores groupBy.
Median seconds each deal took to move from stageA to stageB (target="stageA->stageB").
Share of terminal deals that were won — requires the outcome mapping.

Lead-band: share of conversations ever bound to a non-Deal AOP that were later reassigned to a Deal-bound AOP (a real AOP change, e.g. Vooma's Lead AOP → Deals AOP at qualification) — "lead → opp conversion". Deals-only conversations (never non-Deal-bound) are excluded, same as win_rate excludes non-terminal deals. No outcome mapping needed — the AOP's own boundObjectApiName is the terminal signal, not a status value.
Share of OPEN deals (requires outcome) whose last outbound touch (email or meeting) is older than target days (default 10) — a never-contacted deal always counts as dropped.

Median days since the last outbound touch, over OPEN deals (requires outcome) that have EVER been touched — never-contacted deals are excluded (see deals_dropped for that fact). target is unused (the day-threshold only gates deals_dropped/gave_up_count).

Average number of outbound emails in a stalled, unanswered chain — a run of outbound sends since the last inbound reply (or ever, if none) whose last send is at least target days old (default 10). No outcome mapping needed.

Average COUNT of populated fields on the OPEN pipeline (requires outcome, redefined 2026-09-29): the 4 native buyer fields (company, contact, deal_value, next_step — target optionally narrows this subset, default all four) PLUS every custom field that deal's own rep has actually live-synced from their CRM (resolved per rep, not a fixed list — see queryHygieneSamples). A raw count, not a percentage: the real denominator varies per rep.

Median distinct REAL external contacts per deal in the OPEN pipeline (requires outcome, redefined 2026-09-29), from crm_conversation_contacts — excludes the org's own staff (its configured domains) and known automated/vendor senders (a calendar-notification alias, a document-signing relay, a sales-engagement tool, etc.); a real contact on a personal email domain still counts. A deal with no qualifying contact is a real 0, not omitted.

Median days since the earliest tracked event on each OPEN deal (requires outcome) — a live snapshot of pipeline staleness, not historical time-to-close. Replaces time_between_stages as deal_progression's real source: that one needs a stageA->stageB target this schema has nowhere to carry, and even with one only ~23% of closed deals at a real org had a usable stage-transition timestamp. A deal with no tracked event at all has no computable age and is excluded, not counted as 0.

Real SUM of deal_value across OPEN deals quiet past the quiet-gap threshold (requires outcome; target is an optional day-threshold override, default 10, same convention as deals_dropped/quiet_gap/gave_up_count) — the same stalled-deal population as deals_dropped, summed by dollar value instead of counted. A stalled deal with no deal_value contributes 0, not excluded.

Live CRM closed-won amount and count by currency in an explicit close-date window. Requires exactly one filter.reps user, from/to, and crmReporting.timezone. Uses mapped ACV and provider closed flags; no Cedar fallback. Includes verified provider deal inventory and missing-amount count.
Live CRM open amount and count by currency closing in an explicit window. Same required rep/window/timezone and verified inventory as crm_won_amount; no Cedar fallback.

Real SUM of deal_value across OPEN deals that actually have one (requires outcome) — the performance report's former headline "total pipeline" figure (superseded by won_pipeline/avg_acv as the headline tile, 2026-09-30, but still real and independently useful). A deal with no positive deal_value is EXCLUDED, not zero-filled: unlike stalled_deal_revenue, this can't legitimately count a dollar figure nobody has.

Total dollar value of CLOSED-WON deals in the window (requires outcome), summing deal_value over deals with a real (non-null, non-zero) deal_value. Shares its sample set with avg_acv (same deals, reduced via sum instead of mean).

Average deal_value across CLOSED-WON deals in the window (requires outcome), over deals with a real (non-null, non-zero) deal_value. Shares its sample set with won_pipeline (same deals, reduced via mean instead of sum).

Average taxonomy-atom strength across every list-field atom whose field_id matches target (a family glob, e.g. "coaching.discovery.*" or "coaching.followup.rs*") — the ONE metric that aggregates the sub-event taxonomy rather than crm_conversations/crm_events. Atoms with no strength score are excluded, never counted as 0. No outcome mapping needed.

notes: This catalog covers EVENT and DEAL metrics, plus ONE taxonomy-ATOM metric: "judged_strength" (average strength across every list-field atom whose field_id matches a target family glob, grouped by rep/deal/month and windowed by date like any other metric here). What is still NOT here: per-criterion distributions, counting occurrences, or aggregating a non-strength payload key — those still need `run-sql`, which also gives readable rep names and arbitrary per-deal normalization this catalog never will. Start with the `taxonomy-fields` tool to learn which fields exist, then load-skill("run-sql") for anything "judged_strength" cannot express.
Every row returns { group, value, n, sampleIds } — n is the sample size, sampleIds (capped at 50) point back to the atoms/events summarized.
groupBy:"outcome" and metric "win_rate" both REQUIRE an agent-supplied outcome:{ won:[...], lost:[...] } status mapping.
The filter is the SAME TimelineFilter cube used by the timeline reader; omit conversationIds to scope org-wide.

response_time/followup_time/post_meeting_time/reply_rate/event_count/stage_funnel/time_between_stages already generalize to any AOP as-is — none hardcodes an Opportunity-specific stage/status literal; stage and status vocab are always caller-supplied or read off the AOP's own field definitions. "win_rate" generalizes the same way (see its own note). "aop_conversion" is the one genuinely new Lead-band metric — an AOP reassignment is not a status value on any single AOP's vocabulary.

"deals_dropped"/"quiet_gap"/"gave_up_count" share one `target` convention: an optional positive number of days (the quiet-gap threshold), defaulting to 10 when omitted. "hygiene"'s `target` is unrelated — an optional comma-separated subset of its field keys (company, contact, deal_value, next_step), defaulting to all four.

skills.name: drafting

skills.name: conversation
skills.description: Find/filter CRM conversations, update conversation fields, create new conversations, log events, and reassign ownership. Filtering: analyzes natural language requests, suggests filter configurations, and executes queries to find matching conversations — streams filter suggestions to the frontend for user approval. Load when the user says ''show me'', ''find'', ''filter'', or asks about deals by status, date, priority, or company — e.g. ''show stalled deals'', ''find my Acme conversation'', ''which deals are in negotiation''. Updating: extracts information from communications and updates CRM conversation fields with clean, digestible, high-confidence content that respects temporal context and AOP governance; also creates new deals/conversations, logs meetings/calls/events, and reassigns conversation ownership. Also covers pulling a message in from the user''s LIVE Gmail, Slack, or LinkedIn when they say it belongs to a deal but it isn''t on the timeline — ''there was an email for this conversation from X'', ''we discussed this in Slack'', ''that LinkedIn thread isn''t showing up here'' — finding it in the channel, disambiguating with the user, and attaching it to the conversation; see ''Pulling a missing message in from Gmail, Slack, or LinkedIn'' below.

skills.description: Everything task-related: creating, updating, and canceling personal and sales-conversation tasks; surfacing and ranking follow-ups for today (use when user asks "who do I need to follow up with?"). skills.name: multi-conversation-operations
skills.description: Required before batch operations across 3+ conversations — drafting emails for many deals, updating fields in bulk, or any task that processes multiple conversations individually. Provides concurrency limits and correct patterns.

skills.name: customer-support
skills.description: Report a problem to the Cedar team when the user sends the reserved phrase "flag this" — a signal that something went wrong or was unexpected. Call send-user-feedback immediately with a full debug snapshot: the current working context conversation (id, name), a summary of the recent chat messages in this thread, what action was last taken or what the agent last said, and any relevant state. The goal is to give the Cedar team enough context to reproduce or understand the issue.

skills.name: external-systems
skills.description: Connect to and interact with external, non-Cedar systems. Three paths: MCP-connected integrations (Notion, outreach trackers, custom tools) via call-mcp-tool; Cedar-integrated providers (Google, Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Stripe); and credentials the user stored themselves (Xero, Microsoft Graph, an internal API). The last two both go through get-provider-credentials, then an HTTP caller (run-code-executor in the background, native Bash in chat). Load when the user wants to read from or write to any external system.

skills.name: connected-systems
skills.description: Guidance for interacting with a user's external systems (HubSpot, Salesforce, Attio, Notion, custom tools, etc.) from a Claude session connected to Cedar. Load when the user asks you to read from or write to any system outside Cedar itself. Tells you which systems the user has connected in Cedar and what to do if you don't already have a working tool for the one they need.

skills.name: research
skills.description: Read your LinkedIn network and post reactors; look up external information about people and companies — structured profiles (LinkedIn, headcount, funding) via configured enrichment providers (Crustdata by default for rich research), real-time web/news search, and full page content fetching.

skills.name: documents
skills.description: Read, write, and search Cedar Docs — persistent agent memory for deal intelligence, research, working memory/task canvases, and meeting prep. Also load for complex multi-step tasks or when the user says "remember this".

resources.name: agenda-format
resources.title: agenda-format
resources.description: Markdown grammar for writing to the user daily agenda doc. Load before any write-document call targeting user/agendas/. The parser is strict — follow the format exactly and preserve user-added tasks.

skills.name: tables
skills.description: Build and drive a Cedar TABLE — a row-addressed spreadsheet an agent fills. Load before reading or writing ANY table document, and whenever a task has N independent units of work: designing the columns and their fill instructions with the user, binding columns to live Cedar data (`conversation.stage`, `conversation.fields.<key>`), sourcing rows from a query or an import, and fanning out one agent per row to fill them in parallel.

skills.name: notifications
skills.description: Send notifications to the user via Slack DM, Slack channel, iMessage, or WhatsApp. Use when the automation needs to deliver a message or report.

skills.name: cedar-configuration
skills.description: The foundational skill for anything related to CONFIGURING, DEBUGGING, or UNDERSTANDING Cedar — its data, or its outputs. Load it at the START of almost any task, before other skills or tools. Covers: how executions/runs work, integrations & sync (why something did or didn't sync or happen), ownership and participant semantics, playbooks/AOPs and how their trigger blocks run, the Knowledge Base, company background, CRM field mappings and conversation fields, draft analytics, and where agent output (drafts, field updates, tasks, summaries) goes. It is Cedar's CONFIGURATION surface (the PLAYBOOK.md document is the primary control — read it to understand behavior, edit it to change behavior; playbook design/optimization, org vs. user split, IGNORE rules, full account design/redesign) AND its DATA-REPAIR surface (fixing a broken conversation, merging/moving/de-duplicating deals, reassigning AOPs, reproducing a missing draft or task). Use it for anything that requires understanding or changing how Cedar behaves or what it produced — and as baseline system context even when merely reading Cedar's data.

resources.name: choosing-a-trigger
resources.title: Choosing a Trigger
resources.description: Load when deciding WHEN a rule should run, or when a rule fires too often — first, when timing is the unknown; when whether it is POSSIBLE is the unknown, check that first (agent-capabilities, limits-and-escalation). Covers the trigger ladder, gates that bind only in playbook prose, conditions no event can observe, and dedup. NOT for a live agent that is not firing — see diagnose-and-repair.

resources.name: building-an-agent
resources.title: Building an Agent
resources.description: Load when ready to WRITE a subagent, after when-it-runs is settled: routing by capability, sizing a rule before arming it, proving every call before it is persisted, upsert-vs-patch, wiring the ref last. NOT for deciding when it runs (choosing-a-trigger), what an existing agent is allowed to do (agent-capabilities), or XML syntax (playbook-anatomy).

resources.name: agent-capabilities
resources.title: Agent Capabilities
resources.description: Load first for "why can't Cedar/an agent do X?", including CRM deal creation, before assuming a Cedar-wide limit. Check system-agent allowlists versus custom-agent connection scopes. Also load before assigning work to an existing agent. NOT for authoring (building-an-agent); confirmed Cedar-wide limits go to limits-and-escalation.

resources.name: external-writes
resources.title: External Writes
resources.description: Load before creating an OBJECT in a connected system (a HubSpot or Salesforce task, note or record, a Slack channel, an API call) or before blocking Cedar from writing to certain CRM deals (dealWriteGuard). Covers native tools vs MCP vs credentials. NOT for a Cedar field that syncs to a CRM property (fields-and-values); NOT for Cedar's own tasks, drafts or Slack output (surfaces-and-delivery).

resources.name: surfaces-and-delivery
resources.title: Surfaces & Delivery
resources.description: Load for Cedar output destinations: Slack, drafts, docs, buttons, tasks and Execute handoffs. Also first for human input before drafting ("let me paste notes in"): end the run, collect input, then start another. Confirm destination support before scope-and-sharing. NOT for external CRM objects (external-writes) or legal field/task values (fields-and-values).

resources.name: scope-and-sharing
resources.title: Scope & Sharing
resources.description: Load when a rule might apply to more than the requester — even if they did not say so — and before copying one to another: it fails silently if it references collateral, a field, or a CRM mapping that exists only at the original scope. Covers org vs user, admin cross-user edits, inheritance. Decides WHETHER something is shared, after surfaces-and-delivery confirms the agent can hold it.

resources.name: voice-and-preferences
resources.title: Voice & Preferences
resources.description: Load when a user states a standing rule about HOW Cedar should write or behave — tone, a sign-off, phrases to avoid, "always/never/from now on", "remember that". Covers where a durable preference persists beyond the conversation. NOT for composing one message now (no resource); NOT for reference content like pricing or a deck (knowledge-and-collateral); NOT for draft metrics (draft-analytics).

resources.name: knowledge-and-collateral
resources.title: Knowledge & Collateral
resources.description: Load to persist durable reference facts — pricing, product specs, links, decks — or company positioning in company background. Covers KB retrieval, scope, and wiring explicitly requested automatic use. Reference facts alone need no behavior rule. NOT for behavior/tone directives (voice-and-preferences); NOT for field option lists (fields-and-values).

resources.name: fields-and-values
resources.title: Fields & Values
resources.description: Load before creating, mapping, or approval-gating a Cedar conversation field, or when a VALUE must come from a fixed list — task types, task channels, statuses, stages, retired values. Owns which values are legal. NOT for creating an object in an external CRM (external-writes); NOT for button operations or where output is delivered (surfaces-and-delivery).

resources.name: using-and-configuring-extracted-fields
resources.title: Using & Configuring Extracted Fields
resources.description: Load before referencing ANY field by name in a new or edited agent — org-vs-user scope, whether it's actually kept current (`live`), other write gates (ownership, edit-forbidden, approval), who can change what, and aggregating a field across reps. NOT for creating, mapping, or approval-gating a field (fields-and-values).

resources.name: limits-and-escalation
resources.title: Limits & Escalation
resources.description: Load for confirmed Cedar-wide limits or a CRM rejecting a supported write. Covers 30-minute runs, no mid-run input, event veto or cron state, and no playbook-rule propagation; field/mapping propagation exists. First check agent-capabilities for "why can't Cedar/an agent do X?"; design human-input handoffs in surfaces-and-delivery before escalating.

resources.name: diagnose-and-repair
resources.title: Diagnose & Repair
resources.description: Load for anything that ALREADY happened and went wrong: a missing draft, email or deal, a field that did not update, output that should not exist, an agent that is live but never fired, "why did/didn't Cedar do X". Owns reading executions, sync symptom-to-cause, the repair spine and the fix primitives. NOT for designing a rule that does not exist yet (choosing-a-trigger).

resources.name: playbook-anatomy
resources.title: Playbook Anatomy
resources.description: Load for playbook XML syntax, trigger/ref placement, subagent frontmatter, path shortcuts (#chat-agent reads/writes personal chat instructions without an AOP), manifests and document writes. WHAT a rule should say: choosing-a-trigger, scope-and-sharing, voice-and-preferences, fields-and-values. NOT for running a handed playbook — see playbook-execution.

resources.name: playbook-execution

resources.description: Load when handed a <playbook_section> or <full_playbook_fallback> block in your prompt, or asked to run or test a playbook for a user. Covers reading and acting on <trigger> blocks, @ tokens and subagent refs at RUNTIME — executing a playbook, not changing one. NOT for editing: what a change should say lives in building-an-agent, its syntax in playbook-anatomy.

resources.name: draft-analytics

skills.name: field-query
skills.description: Discover, select, and query CRM field data (crm_conversation_field_values) for one or many conversations, then present results as a table when they warrant one. Covers competitor mentions, current provider/vendor, contract or renewal details, close/renewal dates or other deal timing, objections, pain points, and any other extracted or custom field — for a single deal ('did Acme mention X') or the whole pipeline ('which deals mentioned X', 'deals closing this week'). Load this BEFORE run-sql, conversation's find action, or conversation-read ever touch crm_conversation_field_values, even when the question also sounds like a plain listing/filter question or the right field seems obvious — filtering on a value still requires knowing which field_id holds it for this org, and a short question is not evidence the concept lives in only one field.

skills.name: deal-intelligence-analysis
skills.description: Analyze a customer's deals to uncover non-obvious, grounded sales insight from the extracted sub-event taxonomy — compare deals/reps, trace how a field (MEDDPICC, objections, next steps, discovery questions…) evolved, find what behaviors correlate with wins, and prove every claim against verbatim source. Load when the user asks *why* deals are won or lost, wants cross-deal patterns, rep coaching from real calls, objection / competitor / pricing analysis, cadence or timing analysis, or any question about what's actually happening across their pipeline that needs evidence, not vibes. Runs a hypothesis→proof loop over the Cedar MCP reasoning tools (conversation-read, conversation-analytics, document, run-sql); every number carries a sample size and drill-back, every qualitative claim carries a verbatim span.
